t: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, a member or former member of a uniformed service who initially becomes entitled to retired pay or retainer pay on the effective date of this title shall be entitled to have that pay computed using the rates of basic pay prescribed by the first sect ion of this title.

fable.w: This section only sets how retired or retainer pay is computed for uniformed service members who become entitled on the title's effective date. The word "entitled" might suggest a right held by outside parties, but it is a benefit entitlement, not a right to sue over, comment on, or be consulted about a federal decision. No outside party is involved in any federal decision-making process here.
fable.s: shall be entitled to have that pay computed using the rates of basic pay

qwen_block.w: This section defines the calculation method for military retired pay based on specific statutory rates. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process involving parties outside the federal government. The text is purely administrative and financial, establishing entitlements for federal employees (uniformed service members).
qwen_block.s: a member or former member of a uniformed service who initially becomes entitled to retired pay or retainer pay on the effective date of this title shall be entitled to have that pay computed using the rates of basic pay prescribed by the first section of this title.

opus.w: This section only says how retired or retainer pay is calculated for uniformed service members who become entitled to it on the effective date. No consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue is involved. A member "becoming entitled" to pay could look like an outside party taking part, but it is just an entitlement to a benefit, like an application, not participation in a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines how retired pay is calculated for uniformed service members. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or input from parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities). The uniformed service members are federal employees, and the statute does not grant them or any other outside party a role in the decision-making process regarding the pay rates.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the statute affects members of the uniformed services (who are federal employees), it involves them in a decision. However, the definition explicitly states that federal employees are INSIDE the federal government, and participation requires involvement of parties OUTSIDE the government. Furthermore, this section merely defines a calculation method for pay; it does not establish a process for consultation, comment, or advisory input from any outside party.
